# S-LAUNCH — every Claude Code launch in ccc

Survey of `llms/claude-command-center` at HEAD `ca7e2b5` (2026-10-09). Paths are relative to that repo root. Codex launches (`codex_launch.py`, `codex_switch.py`, `codex_in_claude.py`) are excluded.

## Method

- Grepped `command_center/**`, `tools/`, `codex-in-claude.py` for `claude` tokens in argv lists / f-strings, `--resume`, `--session-id`, `--print`, `-p`, `subprocess.*`, `Popen`, `os.exec*`, `write text`, `async_send_text`, `osascript`, `shlex`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `spawn_ccc`, and the launch helpers' call graph (`_open_tab`, `_tmux_window`, `resume_in_new_tab`, `start_job_*`, `fire_*_in_new_tab`, `relaunch_command`, `session_*env*`).
- Every line number below was re-read with `sed -n` after the grep.
- Checked the installed CLI (`~/.local/bin/claude --help`, v2.1.295): `-n, --name <name>` exists — "Set a display name for this session (shown in the prompt box, /resume picker, and terminal title)". Note the clash: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1` would also suppress the `--name`-driven title.
- Two resolution paths for `claude` matter. Strings TYPED into an iTerm login shell resolve `claude` through the interactive shell, so on Albert's Mac they hit the alias `claude → ~/.claude/claude-wrapper.sh` (which adds `--dangerously-skip-permissions`). `os.execvp` argv and tmux windows (`sh -c`) resolve `claude` on `$PATH` (`~/.local/bin/claude`) and bypass the alias.
- "Leaf" = the line that emits the `claude` token. "Dispatcher" = a site that opens a tab / spawns a ccc subcommand which then reaches a leaf. Both are listed; counts are given separately.

## Shared builders / Phase-1 recommendation

Today there is NO shared argv builder: the `claude` token is emitted in 8 independent places (L1–L8), three as shell strings typed into a shell (L1, L6, L7) and five as `os.execvp` argv (L2-L5, L8). What IS shared is the env policy in `command_center/accounts.py`:

| Seam                                          | Used by                                | Form                          |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `session_env_flags` (accounts.py:535)         | all four seams below                   | dict of non-account env       |
| `session_launch_env_prefix` (accounts.py:562) | L1, L6, L7, T4 (→ L8)                  | shell-string prefix           |
| `session_apply_to_environ` (accounts.py:556)  | L2, L3, L5                             | mutate `os.environ` pre-exec  |
| `pin_environ` (accounts.py:572)               | L4                                     | mutate `os.environ`, no trust |
| `session_launch_env` (accounts.py:547)        | nobody (unused)                        | `env=` dict for Popen         |
| `launch_env` (accounts.py:453)                | resume.py:790 (headless detector) only | `env=` dict, account only     |

Recommendation for Phase 1 (route every launch through ONE argv builder):

1. Add one pure function, e.g. `accounts.claude_argv(*, resume: str = "", session_id: str = "", continue_last: bool = False, model: str = "", effort: str = "", name: str = "", extra: Sequence[str] = (), prompt: str = "") -> list[str]` that always returns `["claude", *flags, prompt?]` with the positional prompt LAST and `--name` always placed right after `claude`. Living in `accounts.py` (next to `relaunch_command` and the env seams) avoids a new import cycle — `terminal`, `snapshot`, `cli`, `park` already import `accounts`.
2. Add `claude_command_string(target, argv, cwd="", subshell=False) -> str` = `session_launch_env_prefix(target) + (cd …&& ) + shlex.join(argv)`. That replaces the three hand-rolled f-strings (L1 terminal.py:455/456, L6 accounts.py:610, L7 snapshot.py:1016) and gives T4 the same prefix.
3. Exec sites L2/L3/L4/L5 call `claude_argv(...)` and keep their `session_apply_to_environ` / `pin_environ` calls.
4. L8 (`session_continue.build_command`) is a separate console script (`claude-session-continue`) that must stay standalone-importable; either have it import `command_center.accounts.claude_argv` (it is in the same package) or add a `-n/--name` passthrough so T4 can forward the name.
5. The `name` value needs a source: the row's `name` / short AIM (`Session.name`, `short_aim.py`), passed down by each dispatcher. The leaf signatures that take loose args (`resume_in_new_tab(cwd, session_id, config_dir, *, no_codex)`) will need a `name=` kwarg; `LaunchTarget` could grow a `name` field so the `SessionLaunch` protocol carries it everywhere at once.
6. Caveat: `--name` also drives the terminal title; if the tab badge is kept via `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1`, `--name` still shows in the prompt box and `/resume` picker, but not in the tab title.

## CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE injection points

Current state: ccc never sets it in code. It appears only in docs as a manual prerequisite for the tab-badge feature: `docs/reference.md:2017` and `docs/hooks.md:143` ("Set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1` (e.g. in `settings.json`'s `env`)").

Single-point injection (recommended): add `"CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE": "1"` to the dict returned by `session_env_flags` (accounts.py:535). Because all launch seams consume it, it then reaches:

| Leaf | How it would arrive                                                                                  |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| L1   | `export CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1;` in the typed prefix (iTerm and tmux branches)         |
| L2   | `os.environ` via `session_apply_to_environ` before `execvp`                                          |
| L3   | same as L2                                                                                           |
| L4   | `os.environ` via `pin_environ` (accounts.py:586 calls `session_env_flags`)                           |
| L5   | same as L2                                                                                           |
| L6   | export inside the `( … )` subshell of `relaunch_command` — does not persist in the user's shell      |
| L7   | typed prefix via `session_launch_env_prefix(pane)`                                                   |
| L8   | inherited: T4 types `session_launch_env_prefix` before `claude-session-continue`, which execs claude |

Caveats for that single point:

- `session_env_flags` docstring says "Today exactly one entry" (`CCC_NO_CODEX`) and its contract is "only ever ADDED"; that holds for the new key too, but tests that assert exact prefix strings (`unset …; export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=…;`) will need updating.
- It should arguably be gated on a config switch (e.g. only when tab badges are on), since it changes behaviour for every launched session; the flag would then live in `session_env_flags` behind `config.load_config()`.
- The headless detector (resume.py:790, `launch_env` — account only, no flags) and `llm.run_custom` would not get it; they need none (no TTY).
- If the user already sets it in `settings.json` `env`, the injection is redundant but harmless.

Per-site fallback, if the single point is rejected: string sites → prepend `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1` right before `claude` (L1 terminal.py:455/456, L6 accounts.py:610, L7 snapshot.py:1016); exec sites → `os.environ[...] = "1"` next to the `session_apply_to_environ`/`pin_environ` calls (cli.py:2452, 2519, 2582, 3193); L8 → inherits from T4's string (terminal.py:503/506).
